summary: Register Telegram Bot API as a Social Core provider adapter with exact-channel bot authorization, text/photo/album/video publishing, HTTPS URL buttons, bounded single-message edit/delete, Task-088 media revalidation, explicit flood-control handling and fail-closed ambiguous-write retry semantics.

impacts.evidence: The adapter receives only a validated tenant-bound connector Account and one configured negative numeric ChatID. Every remote receipt is parsed and matched to that ChatID before edit/delete egress; caller tenant/channel overrides do not exist.

The provider projects only message/chat IDs and normalized state. Bot token bytes are callback-scoped behind SecretAccessor, excluded from method params/fixtures/errors, and provider descriptions/raw envelopes never enter canonical evidence.
Task 041 adds no public TORGNEXA HTTP/OpenAPI operation.
Task 041 adds no EventBus/webhook schema; canonical Task-020 publication events remain unchanged.

Connector SDK v1 gains additive social.post.buttons capability, SocialButton data, and SocialEditor/SocialDeleter capability-specific interfaces. Frozen Connector and Runtime roots remain unchanged and existing providers need no implementation changes.
No migration is added. Task-020 Social Core and existing connector/audit/mapping persistence remain the durable authorities.

Bot/channel identity is exact, Bot API traffic uses host-injected transport, token material is separate from normalized params, media is re-opened through Task-088 immediately before upload, URL buttons require HTTPS, and provider error descriptions are not disclosed.

Task 041 explicitly reviews bounded remote edit/delete capability admission. These interfaces are internal connector operations dispatched only after canonical host authorization against a tenant-bound account; Task-020 remains audit/outbox authority. Album edit, callback buttons and arbitrary destructive/provider surfaces stay denied. Telegram-side deletion limits remain authoritative and never erase canonical evidence.
Task-020 remains Content/Variant/Publication/audit/outbox authority. The adapter returns only bounded Telegram receipts/results and cannot update Core, audit, lineage or storage directly.

Telegram send methods expose no caller idempotency key. Explicit flood-control retry_after is retained, while ambiguous write transport or HTTP 5xx is non-retryable write_outcome_unknown to avoid automatic duplicate posts. Remote IDs are exact channel-bound receipts; Bot API status polling is not invented.
Outbound API authority is fixed to api.telegram.org through host transport. No inbound Telegram webhook/update/callback-query capability is introduced in Task 041.
Telegram envelope/HTTP auth, permission, flood-control and service failures normalize to bounded SDK categories. Manifest pacing is conservative and provider retry_after is preserved when explicit.

Suspend the Telegram connector account or remove the provider route to stop new calls. Existing canonical publication/audit evidence and Telegram receipts remain intact; no migration rollback is required.

Deterministic fixtures/tests cover manifest/auth/config, exact-channel health, text/buttons, photo/album/video, Task-088 revalidation, media limits, channel-bound receipts, edit/delete boundaries, HTTP-429 retry_after, ambiguous-write fail-closed behavior and controlled nil paths; provider report covers all thirteen Task-064 checks.
